title: Flatness under the internal-section module equivalence
statement: Let C be a site, with coefficient universe u containing its object and morphism universes. Assume abelian sheafification exists, its local equivalences are monoidal, and local equivalences of abelian presheaves are exactly locally bijective maps. Assume the abelian sheaf category has coequalizers and is monoidal closed. For a commutative monoid object R, use [def-weil-pbc-internal-abelian-sheaf-module-equivalence] to form its section ring and module equivalence. For every internal R-module M, internal flatness (exactness of both tensor functors) is equivalent to IsFlatOnSite of its section module, in the sense of [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules].

proof.text: Evaluate the internal relative tensor coequalizer on pure integer tensors. Its balancing relation identifies (r m) tensor n with m tensor (r n); its action equation identifies r times a pure tensor with the tensor of r m and n. TensorProduct.lift therefore gives a linear map from the sectionwise tensor presheaf to the section module of the internal tensor, natural in the site object. Extend it by module sheafification.

Conversely, send m tensor_Z n to m tensor_R n and compose with the abelian sheafification unit. The lax tensor comparison of sheaf inclusion is the adjoint of the canonical sheafification tensor isomorphism, so this raw pairing extends uniquely to an internal bilinear morphism. It is balanced: precompose the triple tensor diagram with the raw tensor comparison; that comparison belongs to the localization class and is cancelled after sheafification. The relative tensor coequalizer then produces the inverse map.

Check the first inverse identity after the relative tensor coequalizer and the raw binary tensor comparison. Check the second after the sheafification unit and the sectionwise surjective quotient from integer tensors to R-tensors; tensor induction proves this quotient is epi. Both identities reduce to pure tensors. Naturality in the first module follows from the coequalizer whiskering equation and naturality of the sheafification adjunction. Thus sectionModuleFunctor followed by siteSheafTensorRight is naturally isomorphic to internal tensorRight followed by sectionModuleFunctor. The canonical presheaf tensor and siteTensorPresheaf are isomorphic by the identity on every section tensor; their restriction maps agree on pure tensors. Transport the sheaf tensor isomorphism along this isomorphism. Naturality of the sheafification unit proves the explicit pure-tensor equation, exposed as exists_sectionTensorIso.

An equivalence preserves and reflects finite limits and colimits. Whisker the tensor comparison with the inverse equivalence and its counit to transfer exactness in both directions. The braiding identifies left tensoring with right tensoring. Apply the definition of IsFlatOnSite. All constructions include zero rings, zero modules, empty finite tensors and empty sites.
